//: The 3.9 floor, mechanically. Run it as a SECOND pass:
pyright -p pyrightconfig-hook39.json
It cannot be an executionEnvironment inside pyrightconfig.json, because
those are rooted at a DIRECTORY and the hook now cohabits with the
checker, which requires 3.12 and says so at runtime. One directory, two
floors, so two configs.
The floor is real: the harness runs the hook with whatever `python3` the
PATH resolves to, which on a stock macOS is 3.9.6. A PEP-604 annotation
evaluated at runtime, or a 3.10+ stdlib call, is a hook that raises on
import — and the harness reports that as nothing at all.
`include` is an explicit file list, and the rule for it is: every file a
3.9 interpreter may EXECUTE. That is two entry points, not one. The hook
is the obvious one. The second is `memkit.cli`: the plugin's `bin/memkit`
runs the dispatcher on the same interpreter the hook wrapper resolved,
because only CHECKER-BACKED work needs 3.12 and routing the whole
dispatcher there would put diagnosis out of reach on the machine that
most needs it — a stock-python mac. So `memkit doctor` answers to this
floor as well.
A module either entry point grows an import of belongs here on the same
commit. A module that merely imports one of them does not. Everything
else is covered by pyrightconfig.json, which includes src/ tests/ tools/
wholesale.
